answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a harbor as the anchor of the cost.
